A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same post-hoc reward calibration study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite relocation and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original RewardBench calibration results, AlpacaEval ranking and gameability evaluations, DPO alignment experiments, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds penalty-strength experiments, normalized-penalty and reward-ensemble comparisons, and reward-distribution analyses.

M1.justification: RC-Mean, LOWESS-based RC-LWR, and RC-LWR-Penalty retain their procedures. The calibration constant in Equation 8 and multidimensional calibration already appear in v1. The new normalized penalty and ensemble methods are comparators.

E1.justification: Both versions retain RewardBench, AlpacaEval and ChatbotArena comparisons, LengthBiasBench, UltraFeedback-based alignment, and the same eight downstream benchmarks. The added experiments reuse RewardBench. Translation and summarization enter only the related-work discussion.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix D adds an evaluated z-normalized length-penalty baseline and pairwise normalize-then-average ensembles of nine top-ranked reward models (Figures 15–16). These substantially broaden the comparison methods beyond v1's penalty, calibration, and length-controlled regression baselines.

E3.justification: Existing experimental protocols remain stable. New supplementary settings include ten penalty coefficients from 0.0001 to 0.1, reward z-normalization, and pairwise ensemble evaluation. The new distribution-analysis setting is inconsistently described with gamma = 1.25 on page 23 and gamma = 1.5 on page 25.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds penalty-strength and normalization sensitivity tests (Figure 15), plus model-specific distribution diagnostics under four calibration conditions (Figures 17–26). These substantially extend the analysis of baseline fairness and residual nonlinear length dependence. The earlier bandwidth, calibration-constant, multifeature, and data-efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces kernel-density estimation of joint reward–length distributions in Figures 17–26, adding a descriptive statistical estimation procedure. Ten-seed averaging for the data-efficiency experiments and Table 3's variability reporting remain unchanged; no new confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–14 retain their results, while v2 adds substantial supplementary outcomes. Figure 15 reports a best normalized-penalty gain of 2.75, alongside the retained original-penalty gain of 2.18 and RC-LWR-Penalty gain of 3.11. Figure 16 adds ensemble scores, including 92.25 for the two highest-ranked models, and Figures 17–26 add distribution and correlation findings.

T1.justification: The reward decomposition, independence, density and Lipschitz assumptions, calibration equations, and LOWESS mathematics are unchanged. Calibration-constant scaling and multidimensional regression already appear in v1; v2 introduces no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical correction.

C1.justification: The central claims remain training-free post-hoc calibration, effectiveness across three applications, the 3.11 average RewardBench gain, efficiency, and generality. The revised wording about quantifiable characteristics and preserving desirable bias is consistent with v1's formalization and calibration-constant analysis.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of normalization's benefit to the penalty baseline and why ensembles may retain biases shared by their component models. Its distribution discussion distinguishes reduced Spearman correlation from removal of nonlinear length dependence. The independence-assumption caveat and controllability argument were already present in v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new coefficient grid and comparator construction, but removes v1's code/results repository link and exact verbose/concise gameability prompts. Existing LOWESS settings, hardware, and training-time disclosures remain. Most AlpacaEval procedural detail is relocated from Section 4.2 to Appendix C.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands the focused length-bias review across translation, summarization, reward-model training, alignment, and evaluation. It discusses additional approaches including bucket-based balancing, length desensitization, and meta-rewarding, with new citations such as Hou et al., Liu et al., and Wu et al. The MT-Eval and Arena-hard references are removed.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies RM versus LLM terminology, edits language, rewrites parts of Sections 4 and 4.2, and moves AlpacaEval implementation detail into the appendix. Adding Appendix A shifts the former appendices to B–D, while the main narrative structure remains largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the graphical presentation with the penalty-sweep plot, ensemble heatmap, and four-panel density displays in Figures 15–26. Existing figures and tables are largely retained, with appendix reflow and limited caption edits. A conference-publication header is also added.

improvement.justification: The new penalty sweep, normalized baseline, ensemble comparisons, and distribution diagnostics strengthen the evidence behind the method's advantages, while the original results remain stable. This provides a limited net quality improvement. The benefit is tempered by removal of the code/results link and exact gameability prompts, and the conflicting calibration constants in the new visualization discussion.
